newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan Islamic group calls for leader's release.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan Islamic group calls for leader's release.

text.p: An outlawed Moroccan Moslem fundamentalist group called on Saturday for the release of its 69-year old spiritual leader Sheikh Abdsalam Yassine, who is spending his seventh year under house arrest.

"Seven years have passed since Sheikh Yassine was illegally put under house arrest in Sale...The authories should end their repressive policy and release him," the al-Adl Wal Ihsane (Justice and Charity) movement said in a statement.
Sheikh Yassine was placed under house arrest at his home town of Sale, the twin city of Rabat, on December 29, 1989.
Security men in plain clothes guard Yassine's villa and bar visitors, the group said.
Al-Adl Wal Ihsane was banned in 1990, and six of the sheik's aides, including his son-in-law Abdullah Chibani, were each jailed for two years for belonging to "an illegal organisation".
The group was founded in 1980 and applied for official recognition as a political party a year later. But the interior ministry rejected the demand.
The group describes itself as "a movement against violence of any kind" but its young militants were involved in violent clashes on the university campus in Fes and Oujda in 1992.
A dozen members of the group were sentenced to up to 20 years in jail in 1992 for their political activities.

A group of 27 Moslem students, members of al-Adl Wal Ihsane, were arrested and interrogated by police in recent days in Casablanca for "disturbing public order" while three others were on trial for the same charges.
